historicalReferences: Who can forget the drama of 1966, when Ford's GT40s took a dominant 1-2-3 victory here, solidifying their place in motorsport history?
The 1969 12 Hours of Sebring saw Mario Andretti win in a Ferrari 312P after a dramatic late-race pass, a testament to his skill and determination.
In 1970, the Porsche 908 of Peter Gregg and Steve McQueen took a hard-fought second place, a story that has become legendary.
The infamous sinkhole that developed in the middle of the track in 2013 added another chapter to Sebring's unpredictable history.
Sebring has hosted countless classic sports car battles, from the Porsche 962 era to the more recent Corvette vs. Ferrari showdowns.
The spirit of Briggs Cunningham, a pioneer of American motorsport, lives on at Sebring, a track he helped shape and popularize.
The bumpy surface has claimed many victims over the years, forcing drivers and engineers to adapt and overcome its unique challenges.
Sebring's history is intertwined with aviation, the circuit built on the site of a former World War II airbase.
The 12 Hours of Sebring has been a proving ground for new technologies and innovations, pushing the boundaries of automotive engineering.
The Joest Racing team's dominant performances in the late 1990s and early 2000s cemented their place in Sebring's illustrious history.
